title: Mobileye gains first TÜV SÜD inspection certificate for AEB
summary: Independent audit by TÜV SÜD confirms Mobileye’s automatic emergency braking development process conforms with ISO 21448
body_markdown:
JERUSALEM, October 22, 2026 — Mobileye, a global leader and pioneer in advanced driving assistance tech, has achieved the first inspection certificate from safety auditor TÜV SÜD for its automatic emergency braking development, a new milestone that reflects the increasing impact of the technology in saving lives around the world.


The independent audit by TÜV SÜD inspected that Mobileye’s AEB development process conforms with ISO 21448, the international Safety of the Intended Functionality, or SOTIF, standard for automotive software. The assessment reviewed Mobileye’s AEB development process and the measures used to identify, evaluate and mitigate risks that can arise even when a system is operating as designed. These include the limitations inherent in sensors, perception systems and the real-world conditions in which advanced driver-assistance systems operate.


In a rapidly evolving driver-assistance market, safety validation requires more than extensive road experience or accumulated driving distance. Mobileye builds its approach on disciplined, documented and independently assessed practices designed to identify and address foreseeable risks before deployment. TÜV SÜD’s inspection certificate provides third-party confirmation that Mobileye’s AEB development process meets the requirements of ISO 21448.


AEB is designed to help mitigate or avoid certain frontal collisions by warning the driver and, when appropriate, automatically applying the brakes. Because the function must interpret a wide range of road users, objects and driving environments, its safety depends not only on the absence of hardware or software faults, but also on a structured approach to the intended functionality of the system. TÜV SÜD’s inspection certificate places Mobileye’s longstanding AEB safety-development practices in the framework of ISO 21448, raising the industry standard for safety development processes.


“Mobileye has developed and deployed driver assistance technology for more than two decades, and safety has always been central to how we design and validate these systems,” said Almog Shany, Safety Officer at Mobileye. “TÜV SÜD’s inspection certificate provides an independent view of the rigor behind that process and gives our customers additional confidence in the safety approach supporting our AEB function. Independent validation helps build trust by providing an objective review of repeatable processes, systematic risk assessment and clear engineering accountability for safety.”


The assessment is specific to Mobileye’s AEB development process. At the same time, the underlying safety processes assessed by TÜV SÜD are part of Mobileye’s broader approach to developing driver-assistance and autonomous-vehicle technologies. SOTIF complements functional-safety disciplines by addressing hazards that may result from performance limitations or reasonably foreseeable misuse, rather than failures alone. As driver-assistance functions become more capable and operate in increasingly varied conditions, this distinction is becoming more important for automakers, suppliers and regulators.


Mobileye previously received a TÜV SÜD recommendation for its[Safety Management System for SAE Level 4 autonomous systems](https://www.mobileye.com/blog/t%C3%BCv-s%C3%BCd-certifies-mobileyes-av-safety-approach-for-sae-level-4/) , covering Mobileye’s safety-management framework for autonomous vehicles using the[Mobileye Drive™](https://www.mobileye.com/products/drive/) system.
